claim_text: Apple's System Status page lists Nov 17 incidents for iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), App Store, AppleCare on Device, Apple Business, Apple School Manager, Schoolwork and the Volume Purchase Program, all now marked resolved.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Apple's own status page, read Nov 18, lists each of these services with a resolved outage, issue or performance entry dated the day before.
notes: The page shows 'Yesterday' relative to its Nov 18 last-updated time, so the entries are Nov 17. corroborated_by: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/apple-services-including-icloud-app-store-and-apple-music-hit-by-outage/

claim_text: Per Apple's status page, AppleCare on Device problems began at 11:15 AM ET; iCloud Account & Sign In, iCloud Mail, iCloud.com, the App Store and the Volume Purchase Program at 11:45 AM ET; Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork at 1:40 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page gives a start time for each Nov 17 entry; times are Eastern per the page's last-updated line.

claim_text: All Nov 17 consumer-service entries on Apple's status page are marked resolved, the last by 5:00 PM ET; outlets reported every service showing available between about 5:24 PM and 6 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page shows end times for each Nov 17 entry, with the latest at 5:00 PM ET.
notes: USA Today saw all services available at 5:24 PM ET; an Apple spokesperson told CBS News services were green at about 5:46 PM ET; TechCrunch and NBC News said all were resolved by 6 PM ET. corroborated_by: https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/2026/11/17/apple-services-outage/92827849007/ corroborated_by: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/apple-outage-icloud-apple-pay-services/

claim_text: User reports on Downdetector began around 11:30 to 11:40 AM ET and jumped into the thousands around 12:15 to 12:30 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: USA Today reports Downdetector Apple Pay reports spiking at about 11:40 AM ET and peaking about 12:15 PM ET.
notes: Engadget, a separate outlet, reports first reports around 11:30 AM ET and thousands around 12:29 PM ET. Downdetector counts are user-submitted and do not measure every affected user. corroborated_by: https://www.engadget.com/2319504/icloud-and-other-apple-services-are-down-in-an-apparent-outage/

claim_text: Downdetector showed about 2,300 Apple Pay reports in the US around 12:20 PM ET and about 1,800 iCloud reports at the peak.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reuters cites these Downdetector counts and times.
notes: Single outlet for these exact figures. Downdetector counts are user-submitted.

claim_text: Apple Support had more than 13,000 Downdetector reports as of 1:44 PM ET.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Lifehacker reports the count and time from Downdetector.

claim_text: Apple said: "Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We're working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible."
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Reuters quotes an Apple spokesperson with this statement.
notes: USA Today says the statement was given to it directly; CBS News quotes the spokesperson. Bloomberg was first to receive it. corroborated_by: https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/2026/11/17/apple-services-outage/92827849007/ corroborated_by: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/apple-outage-icloud-apple-pay-services/

claim_text: An internal Apple update caused the outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Bloomberg reports Apple's statement that an internal update caused the outages.
notes: Rests only on Apple's own statement, relayed by many outlets (they count as one source). Apple has published no root cause or technical detail.

claim_text: Apple has not said which internal update failed or what went wrong technically.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Mac Observer reports Apple has not disclosed which update caused the failure or the technical problem behind it.

claim_text: Apple said the outage was not caused by a cyberattack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CBS News reports an Apple spokesperson said the issues were not the result of a cyberattack.
notes: Reuters separately reports Apple said the issue was not caused by a cyberattack. Bloomberg, MacRumors, AppleInsider and Macworld relay the same denial. corroborated_by: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/apple-works-to-restore-services-after-outage-caused-by-internal-update-5033945

claim_text: The Apple outage was a cyberattack or hack.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: TechCrunch reports users on social media speculating about a cyberattack, given the week's other outages.
notes: No credible source has claimed a hack, and we found no evidence of one. Apple denies it (c010). The Nov 18 White House statement says no recent tech outage was a cyberattack but does not name Apple. Not labeled Debunked because the only Apple-specific denial is Apple's own.

claim_text: The week's outages, including Apple's, were a coordinated cyberattack or the work of a hostile actor.
label: Debunked
why_it_supports: The White House says officials see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity or malign actor behind the recent tech outages, and that they are separate incidents.
notes: This is the US government's account, not an independent technical analysis. BBC News reports the Secretary of State said there was 'zero evidence' the outages are linked and lists Apple's among them. corroborated_by: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crkgvxxwpwz2o

claim_text: Apple's internal employee systems, including its staff portal, internal sign-in system and remote-work VPN, went down.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Bloomberg reports this from people with knowledge of the matter.
notes: Anonymous sourcing; AppleInsider and MacRumors relay Bloomberg's report (same source).

claim_text: Apple retail store systems were disrupted, and some stores could not complete purchases.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: NBC News reports employees at Apple stores in New York and Chicago said internal software stopped working and they could not complete purchases or make appointments.
notes: Bloomberg separately reports stores around the world were affected. The worldwide scope rests on Bloomberg alone (Reported). corroborated_by: https://www.cnbctv18.com/technology/apple-works-to-fix-systems-after-update-caused-internal-retail-and-icloud-outages-20036375.htm

claim_text: Some users could not activate new iPhones.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Yahoo Tech reports users saying they could not activate new iPhones.
notes: Based on user reports; TechCrunch and Engadget cite similar user reports.

claim_text: Some App Store Connect developer outages were still open after 7:10 PM ET on Nov 17.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: AppleInsider reports Apple's Developer System Status page showed two App Store Connect outages still ongoing after other issues were resolved by 7:10 PM ET.
notes: We could not read the Developer System Status page directly (its content loads by script).

claim_text: A separate App Store in-app purchase problem ran from 5:28 to 6:46 AM ET on Nov 17, before the main outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: AppleInsider reports this earlier resolved entry on Apple's status pages.
notes: Not visible on the consumer status page as read Nov 18. No source links it to the main outage.

claim_text: Apple's status page lists a separate Stocks outage on Nov 18, from 10:52 AM to 5:55 PM ET, now resolved.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The status page shows a resolved Stocks outage dated Nov 18.
notes: No source links it to the Nov 17 outage, and no outlet had reported it when we checked.
